items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 8.2.1 at source lines 801-802: if A is n-connected then its suspension is (n+1)-connected, proved across source lines 805-870. The proof first has to translate the goal into contractibility of trunc(n+1)(1 sqcup^A 1) (source line 809) and then invoke that truncation of a pushout cocone is a pushout among truncated types to move to the diagram whose vertices are all the point (source lines 811-821). The load-bearing part is the verification that the point is a pushout of that diagram: the cocone type has to be rewritten as Sm{x:E}{y:E}(x =_E y) in two steps, first using that trunc(n+1)A is n-connected while the path type of an (n+1)-truncated E is n-truncated (source lines 840-845), and then using that E is equivalent to that total space (source lines 851-857). Only after that chain can uniqueness of pushouts be applied (source lines 867-869). The statement records none of this: the reduction to a pushout and the two truncation-level bookkeeping steps are the content.
